text:
Anthony Cirelli has a Stanley Cup ring from each of Tampa Bay's back-to-back titles and a reputation as the center you send out when you need the other team's best players to have a quiet night. This season he has been doing his job and not getting paid for it on the scoresheet. Tampa Bay controls 59% of the 5v5 chances when he is on the ice, and he is about five points better than his team without him, but his teammates have scored 6.7 fewer goals than those chances deserve. That kind of gap almost always closes.

His own shooting is the opposite story: five goals on about three and a half goals' worth of chances, slightly hot. His ice time over the last ten games is down more than a minute from his usual, which is worth keeping an eye on for a player whose value depends on the hard minutes. CBS Sports noted six points in six games, and we think that is the start of the correction rather than a hot spell. Our projection puts him around 57 points, ahead of the 52 he scored last season.
headline: Cirelli is owed some goals
